newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade on Monday with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. National Association of Purchasing managers (NAPM) January index, dealers said.
The January NAPM index is forecast to have eased to 53.0 percent compared with last December's 54.0 percent.
Dealers said the market was also waiting for today's release of the U.S. December personal income/consumption and construction spending data.

Personal income for December is expected to show an increase of 0.8 percent against a 0.5 percent gain reported in November while personal consumption is expected to be unchanged from November's 0.5 percent rise.
December construction spending is expected to show a fall of 0.7 percent versus a 1.9 percent increase reported in November.

"Rates were steady to easier this morning on some position adjustments. But some people are waiting for possible direction from tonight's release of the NAPM index, personal income and consumption and construction spending figures," a local dealer said.
